claim: sops-nix system module decrypts secrets to non-persistent /run/secrets and supports per-secret ownership via owner/group so secret file ownership can match the service user, plus restartUnits to restart/reload units when a secret changes
stance_target: system-service host class: credentials delivered to /run/secrets with per-secret owner wiring and restart-on-change
quoted_support: the sops-nix system module decrypts secrets to the system non-persistent /run/secrets ... sops.secrets.example-secret.owner = config.users.users.nobody.name; ... restartUnits = [ "home-assistant.service" ];

claim: sops-nix home-manager module runs as a systemd USER service (sops-nix.service), placing decrypted secrets in the user's non-persistent $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/secrets.d, and consumer user services must order after it
stance_target: user-service host class: credentials are XDG_RUNTIME_DIR-scoped and only exist while the user's service manager runs (requires linger for headless hosts)
scope_conditions: NixOS/home-manager with sops-nix home-manager module; requires home.homeDirectory
quoted_support: the home-manager module places them in the users non-persistent $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/secrets.d ... The secrets are decrypted in a systemd user service called sops-nix, so other services needing secrets must order after it: systemd.user.services.mbsync.Unit.After = [ "sops-nix.service" ];

claim: neededForUsers = true exists for the chicken-and-egg case where a secret is needed before NixOS creates users; such secrets cannot have an owner set
stance_target: boot-time credential ordering: secrets needed for user creation precede user-scoped secrets
quoted_support: sops-nix has to run after NixOS creates users (in order to specify what users own a secret.) To work around this issue, it's possible to set neededForUsers = true in a secret. As users are not created yet, it's not possible to set an owner for these secrets.
